title: ACT ON FACILITATION OF MANAGEMENT AND UTILIZATION OF INDUSTRIAL PROPERTY INFORMATION
title_original: 산업재산 정보의 관리 및 활용 촉진에 관한 법률
full_text:
CHAPTER I GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1 (Purpose) The purpose of this Act is to strengthen industrial competitiveness and contribute to the development of the national economy by prescribing matters necessary for facilitating the management and utilization of industrial property information.

Article 2 (Definitions) The terms used in this Act are defined as follows: <Amended on Oct. 1, 2025>
  1. The term "industrial property" means intellectual property collected or generated in the course of the creation, modification, and extinction of industrial property rights defined in subparagraph 4 of Article 2 of the Invention Promotion Act;
  2. The term "industrial property information" means all types of knowledge or data collected, generated, or processed by means of research, analysis, processing, linkage, etc. by the Minister of Intellectual Property in the stages of creation, protection and utilization of industrial property;
  3. The term "industrial property informatization" means the systematic production, management, provision, and utilization of industrial property information to enhance the efficiency of research and development by the public and private sectors or to effectively establish, promote, and evaluate technologies and industry-related strategies;
  4. The term "industrial property information database" means a collection of information systematically organized and processed for users to search and utilize the same;
  5. The term "industrial property information system" means an organized system of equipment and software related to the collection, creation, processing, storage, management, retrieval, transmission, reception, and utilization of industrial property information;
  6. The term "industrial property diagnosis" means presenting systematic strategies for research and development and commercialization through comprehensive survey on and analysis of industrial property and industrial property information; provided, evaluation prescribed in Article 28 of the Invention Promotion Act shall be excluded herefrom.

Article 3 (Responsibilities of the State and others) (1) The State shall devise and promote policies for the systematic management and efficient utilization of industrial property information.
  (2) The State, local governments, and public institutions under the Act on the Management of Public Institutions (hereinafter referred to as "public institutions") shall endeavor to facilitate the utilization of industrial property information in the formulation, implementation, evaluation, etc. of policies related to technology and industry, taking into account the characteristics of each institution, in accordance with the policies under paragraph (1).
  (3) The State, local governments, and public institutions shall cooperate with each other so that policies for facilitating the management and utilization of industrial property information and creating infrastructure therefor can be effectively implemented.

Article 4 (Relationship to other statutes) Except as provided in other statutes, the management and utilization of industrial property information shall be governed by this Act.

CHAPTER II FORMULATION OF POLICIES FOR FACILITATION OF MANAGEMENT AND UTILIZATION OF INDUSTRIAL PROPERTY INFORMATION

Article 5 (Formulation of master plan) (1) The Minister of Intellectual Property shall formulate a master plan for facilitating the management and utilization of industrial property information (hereinafter referred to as "master plan") every 5 years in consultation with the heads of relevant central administrative agencies. <Amended on Oct. 1, 2025>
  (2) A master plan shall include the following:
  1. Basic direction and mid- to long-term development direction for facilitating the management and utilization of industrial property information;
  2. Establishment and management of an industrial property information database;
  3. Establishment, operation, and linkage of industrial property information systems;
  4. Improvement of relevant statutes, regulations, and systems for facilitating the management and utilization of industrial property information and promotion of relevant projects;
  5. Facilitation of development and commercialization of private industrial property information services;
  6. International cooperation related to industrial property information;
  7. Other matters necessary for facilitating the management and utilization of industrial property information.
  (3) If necessary for the management and utilization of industrial property information, the Minister of Intellectual Property may modify a master plan in consultation with the heads of relevant central administrative agencies; provided, if a modification is made to minor matters prescribed by Presidential Decree, such consultation procedures may be omitted. <Amended on Oct. 1, 2025>
  (4) The Minister of Intellectual Property may request the heads of relevant central administrative agencies, the heads of local governments, and the heads of public institutions to submit necessary data or provide cooperation in order to formulate or modify a master plan. In such cases, the heads of relevant central administrative agencies, the heads of local governments, and the heads of public institutions so requested shall comply unless there is a compelling reason not to do so. <Amended on Oct. 1, 2025>
  (5) Matters necessary for the formulation and modification of a master plan shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 6 (Formulation of action plan) (1) The Minister of Intellectual Property shall formulate and implement an annual action plan for the facilitation of the management and utilization of industrial property information (hereinafter referred to as "action plan") in accordance with the master plan. <Amended on Oct. 1, 2025>
  (2) Matters necessary for the formulation and modification of an action plan shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 7 (Fact-finding survey) (1) The Minister of Intellectual Property may conduct an annual fact-finding survey on the demand for, and utilization of, industrial property information in order to secure basic data for the formulation, implementation, and evaluation of a master plan and an action plan. <Amended on Oct. 1, 2025>
  (2) The Minister of Intellectual Property may request the heads of relevant central administrative agencies, the heads of local governments, the heads of public institutions, and related enterprises, corporations, organizations, etc. to submit necessary data or provide cooperation. <Amended on Oct. 1, 2025>
  (3) Matters necessary for the scope, methods, etc. of a fact-finding survey under paragraph (1) shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

CHAPTER III SUPPORT FOR MANAGEMENT AND UTILIZATION OF INDUSTRIAL PROPERTY INFORMATION

Article 8 (Promotion of industrial property informatization project) (1) The Government shall promote projects necessary for facilitating industrial property informatization and promoting research and development of related technologies.
  (2) The Government may provide administrative, technical, and financial support to institutions or organizations promoting industrial property informatization projects under paragraph (1).

Article 9 (Establishment and management of industrial property information database) (1) The Minister of Intellectual Property may establish an industrial property information database to systematically manage industrial property information collected and generated in the course of performing his or her duties. <Amended on Oct. 1, 2025>
  (2) The Minister of Intellectual Property may request the heads of relevant central administrative agencies, the heads of local governments, the heads of public institutions, and related enterprises, corporations, organizations, etc. to submit data or provide cooperation necessary for the establishment and management of an industrial property information database. In such cases, the heads of administrative agencies, etc. so requested shall comply unless there is a compelling reason not do so. <Amended on Oct. 1, 2025>

Article 10 (Establishment and operation of industrial property information system) (1) The Minister of Intellectual Property may establish and operate industrial property information systems to efficiently collect, retrieve, process, and analyze industrial property information and to smoothly provide industrial property information to users thereof. <Amended on Oct. 1, 2025>
  (2) Where necessary for the establishment and operation of industrial property information systems, the Minister of Intellectual Property may request the heads of relevant central administrative agencies, the heads of local governments, and the heads of public institutions to ensure that their information systems are linked to the industrial property information systems. In such cases, the heads of administrative agencies, etc. so requested shall comply unless there is a compelling reason not do so. <Amended on Oct. 1, 2025>

Article 11 (Facilitation of use of classification information) (1) In order to ensure the systematic management and effective utilization of industrial property information, the Minister of Intellectual Property shall facilitate the use of classification information related to industrial property, such as the classification of patents under Article 58 of the Patent Act and the classification of goods under Article 51 of the Trademark Act. <Amended on Oct. 1, 2025>
  (2) In order to enhance the utilization value of industrial property information and encourage active utilization in various sectors such as industry and economy, the Government may prepare and utilize a linkage table between classification information of different sectors, such as the classification information under paragraph (1), the standard classification of industries under Article 22 of the Statistics Act, and the national science and technology standard classification table under Article 27 of the Framework Act on Science and Technology.
  (3) Matters necessary for the procedures and methods for preparing a linkage table between classification information under paragraph (2) shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 12 (Digitization of industrial property documents) (1) In order to efficiently process procedures regarding patents, utility models, designs, and trademarks under the Patent Act, the Utility Model Act, the Design Protection Act, and the Trademark Act, the Minister of Intellectual Property may digitize documents submitted or generated in the course of filing of applications, examinations, trials, retrials, and other procedures for industrial property (hereinafter referred to as "industrial property documents") by utilizing computerized information processing organization and its technology or may engage in similar business affairs (hereinafter referred to as "digitization of industrial property documents"). <Amended on Oct. 1, 2025>
  (2) The Minister of Intellectual Property may digitize applications not submitted in electronic form under Article 28-3(1) of the Patent Act, Article 3 of the Utility Model Act, Article 30(1) of the Design Protection Act, and Article 30(1) of the Trademark Act, or other industrial property documents prescribed by Ministerial Decree, pursuant to paragraph (1), and may include them in the files of the computer information processing organization used by the Korean Intellectual Property Office or the Korean Intellectual Property Trial and Appeal Board. <Amended on Oct. 1, 2025>
  (3) The contents recorded in the files under paragraph (2) shall be deemed the same as those stated in the relevant documents.
  (4) Matters necessary for the methods, etc. of the digitalization of industrial property documents under paragraphs (1) through (3) shall be prescribed by Decree of the Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy. <Amended on Oct. 1, 2025>
  (5) The Commissioner of the Korean Intellectual Property Office may entrust the digitization of industrial property documents to institutions or organizations equipped with facilities and human resources prescribed by Decree of the Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy. <Amended on Oct. 1, 2025>
  (6) Where an institution or organization entrusted with the digitization of industrial property documents pursuant to paragraph (5) (hereinafter referred to as "document digitization agency") fails to meet the standards for facilities and human resources under paragraph (5) or where its executive officer or employee divulges or misappropriates confidential information about industrial property (including industrial property, for which an international application is filed, and a confidential design under Article 43(1) of the Design Protection Act; hereinafter the same shall apply) learned in the course of performing his or her duties, the Minister of Intellectual Property may require that such document digitization agency rectify it; and where it fails to comply with a request for rectification, the Minister of Intellectual Property may cancel the entrustment of digitization of industrial property documents. <Amended on Oct. 1, 2025>

Article 13 (Survey on and analysis of statistics and indicators) (1) The Minister of Intellectual Property shall examine and analyze statistics and indicators related to industrial property and industrial property information in order to utilize them for the formulation, promotion, evaluation, etc. of public and private technology and industry-related strategies. <Amended on Oct. 1, 2025>
  (2) The Minister of Intellectual Property shall formulate and implement policies to improve statistics and indicators under paragraph (1). <Amended on Oct. 1, 2025>
  (3) The Commissioner of the Korean Intellectual Property Office may request the heads of relevant central administrative agencies, the heads of local governments, the heads of public institutions, and related enterprises, corporations, organizations, etc. to submit data or provide cooperation necessary for survey on and analysis of statistics and indicators under paragraph (1). In such cases, a person so requested shall comply unless there is a compelling reason not do so. <Amended on Oct. 1, 2025>
  (4) Where necessary for research and analysis of trade statistics of industrial property, the Minister of Intellectual Property may request the Minister of Economy and Finance to submit data prescribed by Presidential Decree. In such cases, the Minister of Economy and Finance may submit the data as requested, notwithstanding Articles 21 and 22 of the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act. <Amended on Oct. 1, 2025>
  (5) Matters necessary for the target, methods, etc. of survey and analysis under paragraph (1) shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 14 (Use and provision of industrial property information) (1) In order to enhance the efficiency of public and private research and development and to effectively support the formulation, promotion, evaluation, etc. of technology and industry-related strategies, the Minister of Intellectual Property may collect, process and use industrial property information disclosed under the Patent Act, the Utility Model Act, the Trademark Act, and the Design Protection Act, or may provide information collected and processed. In such cases, the use and provision of industrial property information containing personal information shall be limited to any of the following cases, where it is deemed that there is no possibility of unfairly infringing upon the interests of the information subject: <Amended on Oct. 1, 2025>
  1. Where industrial property information is used for the formulation and promotion of policies designed to manage and facilitate the utilization of industrial property information, such as the formulation and promotion of a master plan and an action plan under Articles 5 and 6;
  2. Where information on the status of applications, registrations, etc. is organized and provided;
  3. Other cases prescribed by Presidential Decree as necessary to enhance the efficiency of public and private research and development and to effectively support the establishment, promotion, evaluation, etc. of technology and industry-related strategies.
  (2) The Minister of Intellectual Property may collect fees prescribed by Presidential Decree, which shall not exceed the actual expenses, from a person intending to be provided with information pursuant to paragraph (1). <Amended on Oct. 1, 2025>
  (3) Other matters necessary for the use and provision of industrial property information shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 15 (Provision of information for national security and other purposes) (1) The Minister of Intellectual Property may use industrial property information, for which an application has been filed, or provide such information to relevant national administrative agencies, if necessary for the prevention of leakage of technology, etc. related to national security or significant national interests and protection thereof. <Amended on Oct. 1, 2025>
  (2) Matters necessary for the details of industrial property information used or provided under paragraph (1) and relevant procedures shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 16 (Utilization of information in public and private research and development) (1) The Minister of Intellectual Property shall formulate and implement the following policies to support the efficient promotion of public and private research and development by effectively utilizing industrial property information: <Amended on Oct. 1, 2025>
  1. Survey on industrial property information trends for identifying promising technologies and research and development tasks;
  2. Strategic survey on and analysis of industrial property information during the entire research and development period for the efficient promotion of research and development tasks;
  3. Strategic research on and analysis of industrial property information for the creation of standard patents;
  4. Support for the utilization of industrial property information in the evaluation, transfer, transaction, commercialization, etc. of the outcomes of research and development;
  5. Support for strengthening the capabilities of any of the following persons to conduct survey and analysis of industrial property information:
  a. Researchers in science and industrial technology;
  b. Specialized institutions defined in subparagraph 4 of Article 2 of the National Research and Development Innovation Act;
  c. Public research institutes defined in subparagraph 4 of Article 3 of the Framework Act on Intellectual Property (hereinafter referred to as "public research institutes");
  d. Business operators, etc. defined in subparagraph 5 of Article 3 of the Framework Act on Intellectual Property (hereinafter referred to as "business operators, etc.");
  6. Other matters requiring the utilization of industrial property information for the efficient promotion of public and private research and development.
  (2) Researchers in the field of science and industrial technology, public research institutes, business operators, etc. shall endeavor to utilize industrial property information in the course of research and development in order to improve the efficiency and performance of research and development.

Article 17 (Designation of industrial property diagnosis institution) (1) In order to effectively conduct industrial property diagnosis for enterprises, research institutes, etc., the Minister of Intellectual Property may designate a national or public research institute, a government-funded research institute, a private research institute, or an institution specializing in industrial property diagnosis as an industrial property diagnosis institution (hereinafter referred to as "diagnosis institution"). <Amended on Oct. 1, 2025>
  (2) The Minister of Intellectual Property may fully or partially subsidize expenses associated with industrial property diagnosis conducted by a diagnosis institution, within the budget. <Amended on Oct. 1, 2025>
  (3) Where a diagnosis institution falls under any of the following cases, the Minister of Intellectual Property may revoke its designation or order suspension of all or part of its business for a period of up to 6 months; provided, in cases falling under subparagraph 1, he or she shall revoke its designation: <Amended on Oct. 1, 2025>
  1. Where it is designated by fraud or other improper means;
  2. Where it is no longer capable of conducting industrial property diagnosis;
  3. Where it no longer meets the standards for designation under paragraph (1).
  (4) Any person other than a diagnosis institution under this Act shall not use the title "industrial property diagnosis institution" or any other name similar thereto.
  (5) Matters necessary for the procedures for designating a diagnosis institution under paragraph (1) and detailed standards for taking administrative dispositions under paragraph (3) shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

CHAPTER IV ESTABLISHMENT OF FOUNDATION FOR FACILITATION OF MANAGEMENT AND UTILIZATION OF INDUSTRIAL PROPERTY INFORMATION

Article 18 (Support for research and development for industrial property informatization) (1) The Government shall endeavor to facilitate research and development of technology, services and software related to the management and utilization of industrial property information.
  (2) Where necessary to efficiently promote research and development under paragraph (1), the Government may require relevant institutions or organizations to conduct research and development. In such cases, the Government may fully or partially subsidize expenses incurred therein.
  (3) The Government shall endeavor to ensure that the achievements of research and development, performed in accordance with paragraphs (1) and (2) (including research and development outcomes and research equipment, materials and goods invested or created in the course of such research and development) are transferred smoothly to the private sector.

Article 19 (Nurturing of specialized human resources) The Government may formulate and implement the following policies to nurture specialized human resources related to industrial property information (hereinafter referred to as "specialized human resources"):
  1. Identifying the actual demand for specialized human resources and formulation of a mid- to long-term supply and demand plan;
  2. Development and utilization of education and training programs for nurturing specialized human resources;
  3. Support for creation of jobs for specialized human resources;
  4. Other matters necessary for nurturing human resources specialized in industrial property information.

Article 20 (Awareness and foundation growth) The Government may promote the following projects in order to raise public awareness of the importance of industrial property information and expand the foundation for utilizing such information:
  1. Education on the utilization of industrial property information for researchers in the fields of science, industrial technology, and design, and others;
  2. Identifying and rewarding exemplary cases of utilization of industrial property information;
  3. Public relations for facilitating the utilization of industrial property information and publication of materials, such as periodicals;
  4. Other matters necessary for raising awareness about the utilization of industrial property information.

Article 21 (International cooperation) In order to facilitate international cooperation related to industrial property information, the Government may formulate and implement the following policies jointly with international organizations, and governments, enterprises, organizations, etc. of foreign countries:
  1. Mutual exchange of industrial property information with international organizations or foreign governments;
  2. Support for international joint survey and research related to industrial property information;
  3. Support for the exchange of technology and human resources related to industrial property information;
  4. Support for international standardization activities related to industrial property information;
  5. Exporting or introducing technologies and systems related to industrial property information;
  6. Other matters necessary for facilitating international cooperation related to industrial property information.

Article 22 (Security and quality control) (1) The Minister of Intellectual Property shall formulate and implement security measures necessary to prevent unfair access to and use of an industrial property information database and industrial property information systems or to prevent forgery, alteration, damage, or leakage of any industrial property information. <Amended on Oct. 1, 2025>
  (2) The Minister of Intellectual Property shall take measures necessary for quality control of industrial property information, such as quality diagnosis and evaluation and support for improvement, in order to ensure the accuracy and reliability of industrial property information. <Amended on Oct. 1, 2025>
  (3) Matters necessary for the subject matter, standards, procedures, etc. of quality control under paragraph (2) shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 23 (Facilitation of development and commercialization of private industrial property information services) In order to facilitate the development and commercialization of private industrial property information services, the Government may promote the following projects:
  1. Support for research and development for private industrial property informatization;
  2. Government purchase of private industrial property information services and support for entry into overseas markets;
  3. Holding events, such as fairs, exhibitions, etc. to promote private industrial property information services;
  4. Rewarding exemplary industrial property information service providers and business start-ups;
  5. Other projects necessary for facilitating the development and commercialization of private industrial property information services.

Article 24 (Establishment of Korea Institute of Patent Information) (1) The Korea Institute of Patent Information (hereinafter referred to as "the KIPI") shall be established to efficiently support businesses related to industrial property informatization and establishment of the foundation for utilizing industrial property information.
  (2) The KIPI shall be a corporation.
  (3) The KIPI shall be established by registering its establishment at the location of its principal office.
  (4) The KIPI shall perform the following businesses: <Amended on Oct. 1, 2025>
  1. Support for the establishment and management of an industrial property information database;
  2. Support for the establishment, operation, and linkage of industrial property information systems;
  3. Support for the processing and dissemination of industrial property information;
  4. Provision of industrial property statistics and information retrieval services;
  5. Support for research and development related to industrial property informatization and transfer of the outcomes thereof to the private sector;
  6. Support for the facilitation of development and commercialization of private industrial property information services;
  7. Support for international cooperation related to industrial property information;
  8. Customer support for industrial property informatization, etc.;
  9. Other business affairs entrusted by the Minister of Intellectual Property in relation to informatization of industrial property, etc.
  (5) The KIPI may engage in a profit-making business prescribed by Presidential Decree to raise funds necessary for performing its businesses listed in paragraph (4).
  (6) The Government may provide the KIPI with subsidies to help it cover expenses incurred in the conduct of its businesses and operation, within the budget.
  (7) Any person other than the KIPI under this Act shall not use the name "Korea Institute of Patent Information" or any other name similar thereto.
  (8) Except as provided in this Act or the Act on the Management of Public Institutions, the provisions of the Civil Act governing incorporated foundations shall apply mutatis mutandis to the KIPI.
  (9) The Minister of Intellectual Property shall guide and supervise the business affairs of the KIPI. <Amended on Oct. 1, 2025>

Article 25 (Establishment of Korea Intellectual Property Strategy Agency) (1) In order to efficiently support central administrative agencies, local governments and public research institutes in the formulation of industrial property strategies and conduct of research and development, the Korea Intellectual Property Strategy Agency (hereinafter referred to as the "KISTA") shall be established.
  (2) The KISTA shall be a corporation.
  (3) The KISTA shall be established by registering its establishment at the location of its principal office.
  (4) The KISTA shall perform the following businesses:
  1. Support for survey on and analysis of industrial property information;
  2. Support for survey on industrial property information trends in the research planning stage;
  3. Support for industrial property creation strategies in the research and development process;
  4. Support for the creation of standard patents;
  5. Performance research, analysis, and management for national research and development industrial property;
  6. Policy research, fact-finding survey, and performance analysis related to research and development strategies linked to industrial property;
  7. Other business affairs entrusted by the heads of relevant central administrative agencies in connection with the formulation of industrial property strategies and the efficient performance of research and development thereof.
  (5) The KISTA may engage in a profit-making business prescribed by Presidential Decree to raise funds necessary for performing its businesses listed in paragraph (4).
  (6) The Government may provide the KISTA with subsidies to help it cover expenses incurred in the conduct of its businesses and operations, within the budget.
  (7) Any person other than the KISTA under this Act shall not use the name "Korea Intellectual Property Strategy Agency" or any other name similar thereto.
  (8) Except as provided in this Act or the Act on the Management of Public Institutions, the provisions of the Civil Act governing incorporated foundations shall apply mutatis mutandis to the KISTA.
  (9) The Minister of Intellectual Property shall guide and supervise the business affairs of the KISTA. <Amended on Oct. 1, 2025>

CHAPTER V SUPPLEMENTARY PROVISIONS

Article 26 (Entrustment of business affairs) (1) The Minister of Intellectual Property may entrust part of the business affairs under this Act to a document digitization agency, a diagnosis institution, the KIPI, the KISTA, or other relevant agencies, corporations, or organizations, as prescribed by Presidential Decree. <Amended on Oct. 1, 2025>
  (2) Where the Minister of Intellectual Property entrusts business affairs pursuant to paragraph (1), he or she may subsidize all or part of the associated expenses. <Amended on Oct. 1, 2025>

Article 27 (Duty of confidentiality) No person who is, or was, an executive officer or employee of any of the following institutions, corporations, or organizations shall divulge or misappropriate any confidential information learned in the course of performing his or her duties:
  1. A document digitization agency;
  2. A relevant national administrative agency provided with information under Article 15;
  3. The KIPI;
  4. The KISTA;
  5. An institution, corporation, or organization entrusted with part of business affairs pursuant to Article 26.

Article 28 (Hearings) The Minister of Intellectual Property shall hold a hearing to take any of the following dispositions: <Amended on Oct. 1, 2025>
  1. Cancellation of entrustment of business affairs related to the digitization of industrial property documents by a document digitization agency under Article 12(6);
  2. Revocation of the designation of a diagnosis institution or suspension of its business under Article 17(3).

Article 29 (Legal fiction as public officials in application of penalty provisions) The executive officers and employees of a document digitization agency and those of an institution, corporation, or organization engaged in the business affairs entrusted by the Minister of Intellectual Property pursuant to Article 26 shall be deemed public officials for the purposes of Articles 129 through 132 of the Criminal Act. <Amended on Oct. 1, 2025>

CHAPTER VI PENALTY PROVISIONS

Article 30 (Penalty provisions) (1) A person who divulges or misappropriates any confidential information on industrial property, for which an application has been filed, learned in the course of performing his or her duties, in violation of Article 27, shall be punished by imprisonment with labor for not more than 5 years or by a fine not exceeding 50 million won.
  (2) A person who divulges or misappropriates any confidential information (excluding confidential information related to industrial property, for which an application has been filed, prescribed in paragraph (1)) learned in the course of performing his or her duties, in violation of Article 27, shall be punished by imprisonment with labor for not more than 3 years or by a fine not exceeding 30 million won.

Article 31 (Administrative fines) (1) Any of the following persons shall be subject to an administrative fine not exceeding 10 million won:
  1. A person who uses the name of an industrial property diagnosis institution or any other name similar thereto, in violation of Article 17(4);
  2. A person who uses the name "Korea Institute of Patent Information" or any other name similar thereto, in violation of Article 24(7);
  3. A person who uses the name "Korea Intellectual Property Strategy Agency" or any other name similar thereto, in violation of Article 25(7).
  (2) Administrative fines under paragraph (1) shall be imposed and collected by the Minister of Intellectual Property, as prescribed by Presidential Decree. <Amended on Oct. 1, 2025>

ADDENDA <Act No. 20200, Feb. 6, 2024>
Article 1 (Enforcement date)
This Act shall enter into force 6 months after the date of its promulgation.
Article 2 (Transitional measures concerning designation of industrial property diagnosis institution)
A person designated as an institution for examination of industrial property rights pursuant to Article 36 of the previous Invention Promotion Act as at the time this Act enters into force shall be deemed to have been designated as a diagnosis institution under Article 17 of this Act.
Article 3 (Transitional measures following establishment of Korea Institute of Patent Information)
The Korea Institute of Patent Information established under Article 20-3 of the previous Invention Promotion Act as at the time this Act enters into force shall be deemed the KIPI established under Article 24 of this Act.
Article 4 (Transitional measures concerning Korea Intellectual Property Strategy Agency)
The Korea Intellectual Property Strategy Agency established under Article 55-5 of the previous Invention Promotion Act as at the time this Act enters into force shall be deemed the KISTA established under Article 25 of this Act.
Article 5 Omitted.
Article 6 (Relationship to other statutes or regulations)
Where the provisions of the previous Patent Act, the Utility Model Act, the Design Protection Act, the Trademark Act, and the Invention Promotion Act are cited by other statutes or regulations as at the time this Act enters into force, the corresponding provisions of this Act shall be deemed cited in lieu of the previous provisions, if provisions corresponding thereto exist in this Act.

This Act shall enter into force on the date of its promulgation; provided, the amendment to the statute which was promulgated before the enforcement of this Act but the enforcement date of which has yet to arrive, among the statutes amended under Article 7 of the Addenda, shall enter into force on the enforcement date of the relevant statute and the following amended provisions shall enter into force on the date specified in each subparagraph:

The following amended provisions shall enter into force on January 2, 2026; provided, the amendment to the statute promulgated before the enforcement date prescribed in the main clause, which has yet to arrive, among the statutes amended under Article 7 of the Addenda (limited to parts concerning the amended provisions of items a and b), shall enter into force on the enforcement date of the relevant statute:
a. The amended provisions of Articles 19(4), 23, 29(1)1 and 30;
b. The amended provisions of Articles 12(2), 19(3) and 22 and the proviso of Article 29(2) (limited to the parts concerning the Minister of Economy and Finance and the Ministry of Economy and Finance);
c. The statutes amended under Article 7 of the Addenda (limited to the parts pertaining to the amended provisions of items a and b);
2. Omitted.
Articles 2 through 6 Omitted.
Article 7 Omitted.
Article 8 Omitted.
